summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and transient low-grade fever. Workup including CT scans of the head, abdomen, and pelvis, as well as cardiac enzymes, showed no acute pathology. Her symptoms were attributed to viral gastroenteritis, and she was treated with IV fluids and Zofran with good response. A mildly abnormal urinalysis prompted a course of ciprofloxacin despite negative cultures. Her chronic conditions—including hypertension, neuropathic chest pain, rheumatoid arthritis, and narcotic-treated pain—were managed with her baseline medications. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged. Her narcotic contract was continued, and she was advised to maintain laxative use.
